guitar.evidence: Carlos Santana has played a PRS Santana signature model since the late 1970s/80s; it's his most iconic and longest-associated instrument, though he used Gibson SG and Yamaha SG earlier in his career.
guitar.notes: Simplified to lead with the PRS Santana as primary, since that is the truly iconic/signature instrument; kept others as historical context implicitly.

tone.target: warm Santana sustain with cocked wah vowel
tone.profile: warm Santana sustain with cocked wah vowel
tone.summary: Gate 1 -> Comp -> OD 9 -> V-Wah -> UK SLP -> US Deluxe -> Chorus (optional) -> Plate -> Digital Delay (subtle)

blocks.purpose: Clean up ambient noise and hum.
Achieve smooth sustain and even dynamics for lead lines.
Provide mid-forward tube drive and boost the signal into the amp.
Implement the signature 'cocked wah vowel' sound.
Simulate the warm, mid-forward tube tone of a classic British/American combo.
Mimic the sound of a smaller, focused cabinet (like 1x12 or 2x12) for clarity and warmth.
Slightly boost the mids to enhance the 'singing' quality and cut through the mix.
Add subtle room ambience and sustain without sounding like a chorus or excessive reverb.
Optional subtle delay for added depth (kept off by default to avoid excessive complexity).

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better match the vintage Mesa/Boogie combo sound and enhance sustain.

proposals.reason: Better captures the specified vintage Mesa/Boogie combo sound and focused tone.
